panels.title: CPU Usage
panels.description: Total CPU consumed by the monitoring stack — grafana, prometheus, loki, alloy, blackbox, cadvisor and the short-lived monitoring-init — as a percentage of a single core (100% = one full core; can exceed 100% on multi-core hosts). This is overhead: it competes with the application containers for the same host CPU, so the number to watch is whether observability is starting to cost more than the thing it observes. Expect a low, flat baseline with periodic bumps on Prometheus scrape and rule-evaluation intervals and on Loki compaction. A rising baseline usually means retention has grown, cardinality has crept up, or a dashboard/alert query is expensive — raise scrape_interval, drop unused label dimensions, or shorten retention. Spikes on startup are normal.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Combined memory of the monitoring stack over time. Working Set = active memory that cannot be reclaimed under pressure (this is what counts toward OOM limits); RSS = anonymous (non-file-backed) memory; Cache = reclaimable page cache. Prometheus and Loki dominate: Prometheus holds recent samples in its head block, so Working Set grows with active series count and drops after each head compaction — a sawtooth is healthy, a staircase that never comes back down means cardinality is growing. Cache is normally large here because both write and re-read TSDB/chunk files on disk; that is reclaimable and not a concern. Working Set approaching the containers' memory limits risks an OOM kill (see the OOM Events panel), which for Prometheus means losing the unflushed head block.

panels.title: Network I/O
panels.description: Rate of network traffic in/out of the monitoring stack (bytes/sec). Receive is inbound — scrape responses pulled from cAdvisor, the JMX exporter and blackbox, plus log pushes from Alloy into Loki and browser requests to Grafana. Transmit is outbound — scrape requests, blackbox probes against the gateway and db, and dashboard/query results back to the browser. Expect a steady sawtooth locked to the 15 s scrape interval. A sustained step up in Receive usually means more series or more log volume; flat-zero when Grafana still renders data means scraping has stopped and you are looking at stale samples — check the Alloy and Prometheus containers.

panels.title: Disk I/O
panels.description: Rate of bytes read from / written to disk by the monitoring stack (bytes/sec). Writes come from Prometheus (WAL, then compacted TSDB blocks) and Loki (chunks and index); reads come from serving dashboard queries over older blocks and from background compaction. Because this shares the host's disk with the database, monitoring writes can add latency to db I/O — if Prometheus and MariaDB spike together, that contention is worth breaking up by shortening retention or moving the monitoring volumes to separate storage. A write rate that keeps climbing over days means retention and volume growth are outpacing what was provisioned; check disk headroom before it fills.

panels.title: Uptime (min)
panels.description: Uptime of the most recently started container in the monitoring stack — the minimum across grafana, prometheus, loki, alloy, blackbox and cadvisor (uptimes cannot meaningfully be summed, so this surfaces the weakest link). Red for the first minute, yellow up to 5 minutes, green after. An unexpectedly low value means one of them just restarted: a Prometheus restart can lose the unflushed head block, an Alloy restart creates a gap in collected logs, and a cAdvisor restart creates a gap in every container metric on this dashboard — so a low value here explains gaps you may be seeing elsewhere. Check the OOM Events panel and container logs; a value that keeps resetting signals a crash loop. Note that monitoring-init is a one-shot container that exits after seeding config, so it is excluded here by design.

panels.title: Memory (Working Set)
panels.description: Current combined active (non-reclaimable) memory used by the monitoring stack — the total that counts against these containers' memory limits, dominated by Prometheus's head block and Loki. Green below 2 GB, yellow above 2 GB, red above 3 GB. Adjust these thresholds to your host: the useful question is what fraction of RAM you are willing to spend on observability rather than on the application. If it stays red, shorten Prometheus retention, raise scrape_interval, or drop high-cardinality labels; see the Memory timeseries to tell a healthy compaction sawtooth from unbounded growth.

panels.title: OOM Events (24 h)
panels.description: Total out-of-memory kills across the monitoring stack in the last 24 hours. Green at 0, red at 1 or more. Any value > 0 means the kernel killed one of these containers for exceeding its memory limit — most likely Prometheus or Loki, and it means you have lost observability data for that window, so treat gaps in other dashboards as suspect. If > 0, raise that container's memory limit and reduce its footprint (shorter retention, longer scrape_interval, fewer label dimensions), then check Uptime for the resulting restart. Recurring kills mean the monitoring stack is under-provisioned for the volume of metrics and logs it is being asked to hold.
